Subject: Renewal + capacity uplift (Q2 activation)

Hi Tessa,

We're planning to increase our committed capacity from 50M tokens/month to 150M tokens/month as part of our June renewal. Can you confirm the path to get an executed addendum and updated billing? Procurement would like the renewal paperwork completed by end of May; legal asked for a redline to the MSA/addendum to review.

I've attached our internal request and the current MSA for reference. Key asks:
- Effective date: 2027-06-01 (align with next invoice)
- Billing: prorated for the month of June after signature
- SLA credit clarification for the larger coverage band

Let me know an expected turnaround and if you need anything else from our side.

Thanks,
Jordan Kim
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Corp
(jordan.kim@acmecorp.com)

Attachments: ACME_2027_Renewal_Request.pdf

Jordan — thanks for the heads up and the clear asks. We're excited to expand coverage. Quick plan:

1) I'll kick off a mutual action plan and share a draft addendum (attaching a working draft).
2) Looping in Marissa (AM) to confirm commercials and Laura (Legal) to prioritize the redline.
3) If legal can turn a single pass redline in 3 business days we should be able to hit end-of-May signature.

Marissa — can you confirm the billing proration approach for a 2027-06-01 effective date?
Laura — please prioritize single-pass review and flag any nonstandard terms (data retention, audit rights, SLA band triggers).

I attached: ACME_Addendum_v0.1_redline.docx (working draft).

Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:30:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + capacity uplift — billing/proration question

Laura — forwarding the request and our working draft. High-level commercial guidance: Acme will switch to the 150M committed tier with standard unit price from our current schedule. Billing should be prorated for June based on signature date; if signed before June 1, billing starts June 1 full month. If signed after June 1, charge prorated days.

Two legal asks from the customer side to watch for:
- They want a 45-day term extension option in Exhibit B (we prefer 30).
- They've flagged the SLA credit cap for the new tier — they want a higher cap.

Can you review the redline and advise on positions? Procurement is pushing the May timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(marissa_cole@redwood.com)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:00:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal + capacity uplift — legal first pass

Thanks for the context — I reviewed ACME_Addendum_v0.1_redline.docx and attached ACME_Addendum_Clean_v0.2.pdf with tracked items summarized below. High-level positions:

- Term extension: Accept 30 days but can offer a 45-day trigger only for notices tied to force majeure or regulatory delay — prefer to keep evergreen renewal mechanics as standard.
- SLA credit cap: For the larger tier, we can offer a modest increase (from 1x to 1.5x monthly credits) but not unlimited. Need business sign-off that this is acceptable.
- Billing/proration: Our standard approach is pro rata daily charges if signature occurs during the month. If they require invoice alignment to accounting periods, we'll need to confirm with RevOps.
- Audit/data retention: Customer redline requested broader audit rights; counter with scoped audit (annual, on-site/remote by mutual agreement) and standard confidentiality protections.

I've left a handful of in-line comments where language could expose broad liability (see footnotes in the attached PDF). If Marissa/Tessa confirm the 1.5x SLA credit counter is acceptable, I'll produce a DocuSign-ready addendum and we can circulate to Acme.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
(laura_bennett@redwood.com)
